header: This is the summary that every circular or announcement search reply carries. A precise answer (circularAnswer.ts: a figure with the document's own words) appears only when the text proves one. A reply that has found a circular or an announcement but cannot prove an answer used to show a bare title, so the reader could not tell whether it was the answer. Now I make such a reply always carry a SUMMARY of the best match, and it says plainly when that match does not answer the question.
1. The model writes two to four short sentences from the passages (and says whether they answer the question: `addresses`).
2. Plain code verifies the summary: every number in it must stand in the text of a passage (a figure that is not in the document is refused, as everywhere in this app); no markup; a sensible length.
3. If the model is unavailable, or its summary is refused, I use the OPENING of the best document in its own words (the first sentences), labelled as that. So a summary is ALWAYS there.
I never let anything here throw.

members.name: text
doc: Holds the summary text, or the document's own opening.

members.name: addresses
doc: Says whether the passages answer the question; I keep null when that is not known (the opening of a document).

members.name: via
doc: "model" means the summary was written and verified; "opening" means I used the document's own first words (the model was unavailable or its summary was refused).

doc: I allow the summary no number that is not in the passages (or in the documents' titles and dates) and no markup, and it must be of a sensible size.

symbols.name: openingSummary
doc: I take the first sentences of the best document, in its own words, clean the table markers out and cut at a word. The result is empty only if the document has no text.

symbols.name: summariseFromPassages
symbols.sig: export async function summariseFromPassages(question: string, passages: Passage[], llm: (prompt: string) => Promise<string>): Promise<DocSummary | null>
doc: This always returns a summary when any passage has text; it returns null only when there is no text at all, and then the caller shows the results as before.

behaviours: a good summary is shown as written, with whether it answers the question and the document it comes from
a summary of a document that does not answer the question says so (addresses false)
a summary with a number that is not in the document is refused: the document's own opening is shown instead
markup, links and lists are refused
a summary of a few words, or of far too many, is refused
the numbers in the document's title and date are allowed (the year of a circular's title)
when the model cannot be reached a summary is still there: how the document begins, labelled as that
an unreadable reply gives the opening too
only a document with no text at all has no summary
the opening is cut at a sentence or a word, at most about 340 characters, and without table markers
the prompt gives the question, each document with its title and date, and the rules: only the passages, exact numbers, say if it does not answer
the reply is read from plain JSON or from a fenced block; a reply with no summary is nothing
a weaker reply is summarised from its best one or two circulars or announcements, whatever their match; a holiday note or a person is not
the answer route reads a strong match for a precise answer, and otherwise (or when it cannot be proved) answers with a summary
the hook asks for a summary whenever a circular or announcement was found, except for a search for a person or an ID
the documents a summary is drawn from are not listed a second time below it (its 'Summarised from' line is their link), as for a precise answer
the search window does not ask for a summary for a name or an ID search
